manufacturer_report.body_en:
Lenovo Support Team,

Device: Lenovo, Serial: {{SERIAL}}, Purchase Date: 2026-01, GPU component: NVIDIA with module nvlddmkm.sys.

Issue: Recurrent system instability linked to the graphics subsystem. The system has experienced 6 incidents over 6 months, from 2026-04-22 to 2026-10-23, with a cluster of 4 incidents from 2026-04-22 to 2026-07-21. There are also two hard freezes without memory dumps on 2026-04-30 and 2026-07-24.

Error analysis: 4 available memory dumps attribute the failure to the common module nvlddmkm.sys. Three crashes are DPC_WATCHDOG_VIOLATION (0x133) with parameters 0x1, 0x1e00, 0x0, indicating a consistent DPC timeout path. One crash is VIDEO_TDR_FAILURE (0x116). The presence of both 0x133 and 0x116 with the same module points to the GPU subsystem rather than an isolated driver bug.

Driver versions: The failures persisted across driver versions. Dumps show nvlddmkm.sys driver timestamps dated 2026-02-14 and 2026-03-04. One dump has no driver timestamp available, so its version could not be verified. The update between February and March did not resolve the issue.

Additional context: 3 of the 6 incidents occurred during power state transitions, which may suggest a power-management interaction, but this remains a hypothesis. No disk errors, CPU/memory hardware errors, repeated application failures, or CPU thermal throttling were logged, indicating other major components appear healthy based on logs alone.

Steps already taken: Driver update tested across at least two versions (2026-02-14 and 2026-03-04) without resolution.

Request: Please provide diagnosis for GPU hardware/firmware versus low-level driver-hardware interaction fault, and advise on warranty repair/replacement process. Dumps are retained for further analysis if needed.
manufacturer_report.body_es:
Equipo de Soporte de Lenovo,

Dispositivo: Lenovo, Serie: {{SERIAL}}, Fecha de compra: 2026-01, Componente GPU: NVIDIA con modulo nvlddmkm.sys.

Incidencia: Inestabilidad recurrente del sistema vinculada al subsistema grafico. El equipo ha presentado 6 incidencias en 6 meses, desde 2026-04-22 hasta 2026-10-23, con un grupo de 4 incidencias entre 2026-04-22 y 2026-07-21. Ademas hay dos bloqueos sin volcado de memoria el 2026-04-30 y el 2026-07-24.

Analisis de errores: 4 volcados de memoria disponibles atribuyen el fallo al modulo comun nvlddmkm.sys. Tres bloqueos son DPC_WATCHDOG_VIOLATION (0x133) con parametros 0x1, 0x1e00, 0x0, lo que indica una ruta de tiempo de espera DPC consistente. Un bloqueo es VIDEO_TDR_FAILURE (0x116). La presencia de 0x133 y 0x116 con el mismo modulo apunta al subsistema GPU y no a un error aislado del controlador.

Versiones de controlador: Los fallos persistieron entre versiones del controlador. Los volcados muestran marcas de tiempo del controlador nvlddmkm.sys de 2026-02-14 y 2026-03-04. Un volcado no tiene marca de tiempo disponible, por lo que su version no se pudo verificar. La actualizacion entre febrero y marzo no resolvio el problema.

Contexto adicional: 3 de las 6 incidencias ocurrieron durante transiciones de estado de energia, lo que podria sugerir una interaccion con la gestion de energia, pero esto es solo una hipotesis. No se registraron errores de disco, errores de hardware de CPU/memoria, fallos repetidos de aplicaciones ni estrangulamiento termico de CPU, lo que indica que otros componentes principales parecen estar sanos segun los registros.

Acciones ya realizadas: Actualizacion del controlador probada en al menos dos versiones (2026-02-14 y 2026-03-04) sin resolucion.

Solicitud: Por favor proporcionen diagnostico sobre posible fallo de hardware/firmware de GPU frente a interaccion de bajo nivel entre controlador y hardware, e indiquen el proceso de reparacion o reemplazo en garantia. Los volcados se conservan para analisis adicional si es necesario.

case.user_summary: Your Lenovo has had 6 incidents over 6 months involving the NVIDIA graphics system, causing blue screens and freezes. The problem has kept happening even after graphics driver updates, which points to a likely hardware or firmware issue rather than just a driver bug. Please share the attached technical report with Lenovo support to request diagnosis and warranty repair.

checklist.step: Install system manufacturer's recommended NVIDIA driver (not generic) and document driver versions, use DDU clean-install method
Update and record BIOS/UEFI version, GPU VBIOS version, and firmware settings
Provide hardware diagnostics: GPU stress test (FurMark/3DMark), VRAM test, PSU voltage logs, reseat GPU and power connectors
Provide GPU-specific telemetry: GPU temperature, hotspot, VRAM errors, fan speed and power logs
Provide full driver version history including missing timestamp for 2026-04-22 dump, Windows Update history, and complete memory dump stack trace
Provide Kernel-Power and SleepStudy reports for power-transition incidents

findings.text: 6 total incidents over 6 months (2026-04-22 to 2026-10-23): 4 with memory dumps and 2 freezes without blue screen (NO_BLUE_SCREEN 2026-04-30, 2026-07-24)
Repetition threshold met: 4 incidents within 90-day window 2026-04-22 .. 2026-07-21

3 dumps share identical failure category (2026-04-22, 2026-07-17, 2026-07-21) even with different symbol offsets and different bugcheck params - this means same failure CATEGORY per rules, not proof of same underlying defect as other machines

1 dump is different category but same module: 0x116 VIDEO_TDR_FAILURE on 2026-10-23 - confirms recurring module involvement across two bugcheck types (0x133 DPC_WATCHDOG_VIOLATION x3 and 0x116 VIDEO_TDR_FAILURE x1), both GPU driver timeout failures

Same module nvlddmkm.sys failed across 2 distinct driver timestamps: 2026-03-04 and 2026-02-14; one dump has null timestamp so may be additional version - persistence across driver versions is the strongest argument to escalate to manufacturer as updating driver alone did not resolve
Correlation with power transitions (3/6 incidents during power transition) is flagged as hypothesis only - insufficient evidence to prove power management is root cause vs coincidental trigger
The 2 freezes without dumps have no dump_module evidence; hypothesized to be related GPU hangs that failed to produce dumps, but cannot be proven to be nvlddmkm.sys from this evidence alone
No evidence of single-application cause: dumps show process System and Unity Hub.exe - indicates system-level driver instability not isolated to one app

healthy_components: Disk: No disk errors were logged
Hardware: Windows logged no memory or CPU hardware errors (WHEA)
Software: No repeated application failures logged
Thermal: No CPU throttling due to temperature was logged - note: GPU temperature not logged in this dataset

manufacturer_report.body_en:
Dear Support Team,

Device: Lenovo - please specify exact model, Serial: {{SERIAL}}
Purchase Date: 2026-01
GPU: NVIDIA

Incident Timeline:
The system has experienced 6 incidents over 6 months from 2026-04-22 to 2026-10-23. This includes 4 Blue Screen crashes with memory dumps on 2026-04-22, 2026-07-17, 2026-07-21 and 2026-10-23, and 2 hard freezes without Blue Screen on 2026-04-30 and 2026-07-24. Repetition threshold was met with 4 incidents within the 90-day window from 2026-04-22 to 2026-07-21.

Technical Details:
- Responsible module in all 4 dumps: nvlddmkm.sys.
- Error codes: 0x133 DPC_WATCHDOG_VIOLATION on 2026-04-22, 2026-07-17 and 2026-07-21; 0x116 VIDEO_TDR_FAILURE on 2026-10-23. Both are GPU driver timeout failure types.
- Three dumps share the same failure category (2026-04-22, 2026-07-17, 2026-07-21). The dump on 2026-10-23 is a different category but same module, confirming recurring involvement of nvlddmkm.sys across two bugcheck types. Same category means same failure type per classification, not proof of same defect as other machines.
- Driver versions observed: 2026-03-04 and 2026-02-14. One dump from 2026-04-22 had null timestamp, suggesting a possible third version. The failure persisted across versions, indicating that updating the driver alone did not resolve the issue.
- Processes at time of crash: System and Unity Hub.exe, indicating system-level driver instability, not isolated to a single application.
- Healthy checks: no disk errors, no WHEA memory or CPU hardware errors, no repeated application failures, no CPU thermal throttling logged (GPU temperature not available).
- Power transition correlation was noted in 3 incidents but is considered a hypothesis only with insufficient evidence.
- The 2 freezes without dumps have no module evidence and cannot be proven to be nvlddmkm.sys, but are temporally related.

Steps Already Taken:
- Driver updates between versions (2026-02-14 to 2026-03-04) - issue persisted.
- Basic health checks showed no disk, WHEA, or CPU thermal issues.

Request:
Please provide diagnosis and advise on warranty repair. The persistent failure across driver versions suggests a likely hardware fault in the GPU subsystem that requires manufacturer evaluation. Pending information includes BIOS/UEFI version, GPU VBIOS, installation of manufacturer-recommended NVIDIA driver with clean install, GPU temperature/VRAM/power telemetry, full memory dump analysis, and hardware diagnostics results (GPU stress test, VRAM test, PSU logs, reseat test), plus Kernel-Power and SleepStudy reports.

Thank you.
manufacturer_report.body_es:
Estimado equipo de soporte:

Dispositivo: Lenovo - por favor especificar modelo exacto, Serie: {{SERIAL}}
Fecha de compra: 2026-01
GPU: NVIDIA

Cronologia de incidentes:
El equipo ha presentado 6 incidentes en 6 meses desde el 2026-04-22 hasta el 2026-10-23. Incluye 4 pantallazos azules con volcado de memoria los dias 2026-04-22, 2026-07-17, 2026-07-21 y 2026-10-23, y 2 bloqueos sin pantallazo azul los dias 2026-04-30 y 2026-07-24. Se cumple el umbral de repeticion con 4 incidentes dentro del periodo de 90 dias del 2026-04-22 al 2026-07-21.

Detalles tecnicos:
- Modulo responsable en los 4 volcados: nvlddmkm.sys.
- Codigos de error: 0x133 DPC_WATCHDOG_VIOLATION el 2026-04-22, 2026-07-17 y 2026-07-21; 0x116 VIDEO_TDR_FAILURE el 2026-10-23. Ambos son fallos de tiempo de espera del controlador grafico.
- Tres volcados comparten la misma categoria de fallo (2026-04-22, 2026-07-17, 2026-07-21). El volcado del 2026-10-23 es de categoria distinta pero del mismo modulo, confirmando implicacion recurrente de nvlddmkm.sys en dos tipos de bugcheck. Misma categoria significa mismo tipo de fallo segun clasificacion, no prueba del mismo defecto que en otros equipos.
- Versiones de controlador observadas: 2026-03-04 y 2026-02-14. Un volcado del 2026-04-22 no tenia marca de tiempo, lo que sugiere una posible tercera version. El fallo persistio al cambiar de version, por lo que actualizar el controlador no resolvio el problema.
- Procesos en el momento del fallo: System y Unity Hub.exe, lo que indica inestabilidad a nivel de sistema, no aislada a una aplicacion.
- Comprobaciones de componentes sanos: sin errores de disco, sin errores de hardware WHEA de memoria o CPU, sin fallos repetidos de aplicaciones, sin estrangulamiento termico de CPU (temperatura de GPU no disponible).
- La correlacion con transiciones de energia en 3 incidentes es solo hipotesis con evidencia insuficiente.
- Los 2 bloqueos sin volcado no tienen evidencia de modulo y no se puede probar que sean nvlddmkm.sys, pero estan relacionados temporalmente.

Acciones ya realizadas:
- Actualizaciones de controlador entre versiones (2026-02-14 a 2026-03-04) - el problema persistio.
- Verificaciones basicas sin errores de disco, WHEA o temperatura de CPU.

Solicitud:
Solicito diagnostico y evaluacion para reparacion en garantia. La persistencia a traves de versiones de controlador sugiere un probable fallo de hardware en el subsistema grafico que requiere evaluacion del fabricante. Informacion pendiente incluye version de BIOS/UEFI, VBIOS de GPU, instalacion del controlador NVIDIA recomendado por el fabricante con instalacion limpia, telemetria termica/de VRAM/alimentacion de GPU, analisis completo del volcado de memoria y resultados de diagnostico de hardware (prueba de estres de GPU, prueba de VRAM, registros de fuente, prueba de reasentado), ademas de informes Kernel-Power y SleepStudy.

Gracias.
